did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezekiel is brought to the chambers on the north side of the outer court, opposite the restricted area and the building.
Did you know? The northern chambers are described as one hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide.
Did you know? The chambers are opposite the twenty cubits of the inner court and the pavement of the outer court, and they are built with gallery facing gallery in three stories.
Did you know? In front of the chambers is a passage ten cubits wide, with a path one cubit wide alongside it; the entrances to the chambers face north.
Did you know? The upper chambers are shorter than the lower and middle ones because the structure is stepped and the galleries take up space.
Did you know? The three-story chambers have no pillars like the pillars of the courts; therefore, the upper stories are set back and become shorter.

Did you know? The northern and southern chambers opposite the restricted area are called the holy chambers. There the priests eat the most holy offerings and place the grain offering, sin offering, and guilt offering.

Did you know? The priests do not leave the holy area for the outer court while wearing their ministering garments. They leave their holy garments there, put on other clothes, and only then approach the area intended for the people.
Did you know? After completing the measurements of the inner temple, the man measures the area all around it, on all four sides.
Did you know? Each side of the area measures five hundred reeds, and the wall surrounding it is intended to separate the holy from the common.
